text:
maya: Quick update — kicked off bring-up for sapling-v2-embed (int8, per-channel) on staging. Baseline vs sapling-int8 looks odd for short queries (<=8 tokens): recall@1 down ~3.5%. UMAP shows a thin cloud of low-similarity points. Attaching the quick numbers below.

raj: thx. what batch / microbatch / kv settings? could be batching amplification for short queries.

sara: microbatch=8, batcher=adaptive, kv_cache=enabled. ran the standard shortquery holdout (5k queries). Quick metrics paste: 
```
baseline (bertish-embed v1 float16): recall@1: 0.842
 sapling-v2-int8 (per-channel): recall@1: 0.806
 recall@5: 0.931 -> 0.924
 silhouette score (kmeans k=50): 0.38 -> 0.31
 mean cosine shift (top1): -0.028
```

keith: hmm delta concentrated on query length <=6? any pattern by domain (docs vs short chat utterances)? :thinking_face:

maya: yes, looks skewed to short conversational queries and some code-snippet prompts. Longform doc queries largely unchanged.

lina: have we tried int8 w/ per-channel=off and a fp16 baseline run on the same infra? sometimes kernel selection differs and that amplifies small vectors.

ops-bot: deploy job 8242 started for sapling-v2-embed int8-perchannel on staging (pool=gnode-staging-3). ETA ~6m :gear:

dan: suggestions: run (1) int8 per-channel off, (2) int8 per-tensor, (3) int4 fast quant (eval-only), and (4) fp16/ bf16 match to confirm it's quant artifact not tokenization mismatch. Also sanity-check nearest-neighbor internal distances for short queries — look for centroid collapse.

raj: also run a microbatch=1 and microbatch=2 -> see if continuous batching merges short queries into bigger batches causing prefix cache reuse side effects.

maya: will kick those sweeps now. planning quick A/B comparisons for recall@1/5/10 and silhouette + UMAP snapshots. I[0mll log exact seeds and dataset slice. Posting results in this thread.

sara: one more: export a few example pairs that flipped from top1->top100 so we can inspect qualitatively (often reveals tokenizer edgecases).

maya: yep will include example pairs. quick note: initial qualitative check shows a handful where sapling maps punctuation-only queries to same dense bucket — suspicious.

keith: if you need compute let me know; can spin a small dedicated node to avoid noisy neighbors during numeric diffs.

maya: thanks, will ping. planning to have first sweep summary in ~1hr. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
